name: Schloss Ambras
kurzbeschreibung: Renaissance castle and museum on the southern edge of Innsbruck with the Spanish Hall, the Chamber of Art and Curiosities, the Armouries and the castle park.
beschreibung:
Ambras Castle in Innsbruck lies on the southern outskirts of the Tyrolean capital and is among the most important sights in Austria. It is the only location of the KHM museum association outside Vienna and has been owned by the Republic of Austria since 1919.

Archduke Ferdinand II. took up residence in the complex in 1564 as the residence of the Prince of Tyrol. The upper castle was rebuilt and extended in Renaissance style; beneath the living quarters rose the grand Spanish Hall, the lower castle and extensive gardens. The lower castle housed horse stables, a granary and, step by step, the collections of Ferdinand II.: the Chamber of Art and Curiosities, the Armouries, portraits, weapons and a library. This building, constructed specifically as a “Musaeum”, makes Ambras Castle the first museum in the world: the oldest systematic concept of collecting and presentation can still be experienced at its original location.

The castle park with its paradise garden and medicinal herb garden is freely accessible. The museum is open daily from 10 am to 5 pm and closed in November; tickets cost 18 € on site and 16 € online.
